title: Leveraging Large Language Models (LLMs) for Process Mining (Technical Report)

bias_targets.methodology: Prompting LLMs to generate SQL queries that classify cases into protected and non-protected groups based on age, and then having the models identify procedural discrepancies between these groups in process mining event logs.
Prompting LLMs to generate SQL queries that classify cases based on citizenship status, followed by analyzing process variants to detect procedural discrimination in event logs.
Prompting LLMs to classify cases based on language (German) proficiency using generated SQL queries, and identifying differing process outcomes or treatments in event logs.
Using LLM-generated SQL queries to isolate cases by gender and prompting the models to compare process variants to uncover potential procedural fairness issues.
Prompting LLMs to classify cases into protected groups based on religion using SQL queries and identifying unfair procedural discrepancies in event logs.
Generating SQL queries via LLMs to group cases by years of education, then prompting the models to analyze differences in process execution for procedural fairness.
Prompting LLMs to generate SQL queries that isolate cases based on underlying health conditions, and evaluating the models' ability to detect unfair process variations.
Classifying cases by private insurance status through LLM-generated SQL queries and evaluating the LLMs' ability to identify procedural discrimination in process mining logs.
